Commentary.Commentary: Right then, two unbeaten teams of the tournament will be fittingly locking horns in the final. Are the English fans already singing 'it's coming home' - for the first time since 1998 or will it be India Under-19 extending their domination and adding the fifth trophy to their cabinet? It promises to be a lip-smacking finale on Saturday, 5th February, at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT). You can join us in advance for the build-up. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Cooper Connolly, the skipper of Australia Under-19, says that the Indian batters played really well in the last 10 overs and 290 was a bit too much for them. Adds that they adapted well to the conditions and there are positives to take back home. Mentions that it was a good experience but the only problem was the bubble.

Yash Dhull, the skipper of India Under-19, is also the PLAYER OF THE MATCH. Says that his stand with Shaik Rasheed was the key as they didn't get a good start. Adds that they spoke about batting till the end as they knew that runs would come towards the end. He praises Rasheed for the way he batted right after recovering from Covid-19 and says that he enjoys batting with him. Dhull further says that the finish was good after the big partnership between him and Rasheed. Mentions that the team played well and there is not much that they would want to change.
Presentation time...

Earlier in the match, the initial defensive batting approach of India Under-19 frustrated and tired the Aussies and then their stunning attack at the backend deflated their morale. It was a very cleverly devised plan from India and the execution was top drawer. The batting of India Under-19 in the last 10 overs proved to be the difference. They amassed 108 runs in that period and propelled their total to 290. Yash Dhull and Shaik Rasheed were the chief architects with the bat, scoring handy individual runs and raising a double century partnership.

If we cheekily modify a famous social media meme, we can say - 'Australia's batting against spin, still a better love story than Twilight!' Their senior team struggles against spin and the youngsters also were below-par. They did fare well against Pakistan Under-19 but against the quality of the Indian spinners, they kept on losing wickets. Out of the 10 wickets to fall, 7 were pocketed by the quartet of Nishant Sindhu, Vicky Ostwal, Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Kaushal Tambe as they scripted an easy win in the end.

It's one thing to plan, another thing to execute. India did, Australia didn't - to put it simply. Australia Under-19 did the first part of copying India's batting innings well as they took it slow and steady but the harder part of emulating India's acceleration was nowhere to be found. Instead, the Aussies succumbed under the increasing scoreboard pressure and the Indian boys bowled smartly to not let the intensity drop. Apart from Lachlan Shaw, there wasn't much fight shown by the Aussies and they ended up facing a hefty defeat.

INDIA UNDER-19 ARE IN THE FINAL! A commanding performance from them as they outclassed Australia Under-19 in all the facets of the game. The Boys in Blue advance to their 8th final of the ICC Under-19 World Cup, their fourth consecutive appearance in the finale and they continue to stamp their authority.

OUT! RUN OUT! There it is! There comes the final wicket and India Under-19 are through to the final of the Under-19 World Cup! Shorter and on off. Jack Nisbet miscues his pull to mid off. Tom Whitney wants a single but is sent back by his partner. Rajvardhan Hangargekar though runs in from inside the ring and fires a direct hit at the bowler's end before Whitney can come back in. The on-field umpire raises his finger and India Under-19 win by 96 runs!
Length ball, on off. Blocked out to covers.
Back of a length, on off. Heaved off the inner half of the bat to deep mid-wicket for one.
Short and wide outside off. This time, he misses the attempted cut shot.
Shorter, outside off. Tom goes for the full-blooded pull but misses.
Length ball, on off. Blocked out.
Very full, on off. Pushed to short cover.
Low full toss, outside off. Tom goes for the drive but gets the outside edge towards deep point for one.
SIX! He does it again! Short and on off. Whitney rocks back and heaves it way over the mid-wicket fence. He is having some fun out there.
SIX! OH, MY WORD! That has been smoked! Absolutely smoked! Short and wide outside off. Tom Whitney nails the cut shot all the way over the cover fence.
Yorker, outside off. Tom Whitney digs it out to short third man.
Powerplay 3 time. One extra fielder, i.e. 5 can now be put outside the 30-yard circle till the time this chase goes on.
Back of a length, around off. Nisbet fails to get any bat on it.
Switches back to over the wicket and bowls a shorter one, around off. Jack Nisbet blocks it well.
Wide! Comes 'round the wicket and bowls a short one, wide outside off. Left alone and called a wide.
Fuller this time, outside off. Nisbet misses the drive.
Play and a miss! Shorter and outside off. Nisbet chases it but misses. The keeper is very interested as he appeals for a caught behind but he is the only one doing so.
Very full, on off. Dug out to covers for one.
Back of a length, outside off. Whitney misses the pull.
Jack Nisbet is the number 11 batter. Rajvardhan Hangargekar is back on as well to finish things off.

OUT! DRAGS IT ON! India Under-19 are only a wicket away now! Shaw departs after a well-made fifty. Back of a length, on off. He looks to heave it away to the leg side but ends up dragging it onto the stumps off the inner edge.
Full ball, on off. Whitney pushes it to covers for one.
Very full, on off. Shaw plays it to long on for one.
Short and outside off. This time, Whitney pulls it through mid-wicket for one.
FIFTY for Shaw! He has played well and has deserved this. Short and on off. He pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter, on off. Shaw miscues the heave.
Shortish and around off, Shaw forces it wide of the bowler, towards mid off and retains strike with a single. 10-0-42-3, Vicky Ostwal is done with his spell.
This one is stroked from the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.
Dropped! Nishant Sindhu puts down a sitter. Loopy again, full and on middle, Tom Whitney flicks it aerially to short mid-wicket where Nishant Sindhu fails to hang on to the catch.
Short and outside off, tapped down to point.
Appeal for an lbw! Loopy and full around off, Tom Whitney tries to sweep but misses. He is hit on the front pad, they appeal but the impact appears to be outside off.
Flatter and around off, Tom pushes it off his back foot to covers.

FOUR! Interesting shot! Tossed up, full and around off, Lachlan Shaw goes down for the sweep shot but loses his balance. He goes down but the ball flies up off the top edge. It travels behind the keeper and finds the fence.
Short and around off, skidding away, Tom Whitney punches it to covers for a single.
Tom Whitney walks out to bat.

OUT! STUMPED! Clever bowling from Kaushal Tambe. He pushes this one quicker and wider outside off, Jack Sinfield advances down the track and tries to cut but misses. Dinesh Bana does the rest - smooth stumping. End of a short cameo from Jack.
Commentary.Howout: st Dinesh Bana b Kaushal Tambe

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Jack Sinfield goes against the wind but still manages to clear the fence. Loopy and full around off, Jack kneels and smokes it all the way over mid-wicket.
Flatter and on off, defended to the off side.

Great work by the big quick! Full and around off, it's swept down towards fine leg. The ball races away but before it could reach the fence, Rajvardhan Hangargekar puts in a dive and stops the ball. Saves a run. Excellent commitment.
Change. Kaushal Tambe (5-0-18-0) is brought back.
Short and wide outside off, Jack Sinfield thumps it off his back foot but finds the cover fielder. 9 from the over, the required rate is 9.5 now.
Flatter and a touch shorter on off, Shaw helps it to mid-wicket and picks up a single.
In the air, safe! Fuller and on off, Jack Sinfield again goes for the slog-sweep but this time doesn't middle it well. It goes on one bounce to long on and they take a run.
FOUR! Jack Sinfield trying to have a bit of fun here. Goes with the spin against a full ball and swings it firmly to wide long on for a boundary.
Loopy and full around off, Lachlan Shaw drives it through mid off and takes a run.
Full and floated around off, Shaw sweeps it to deep mid-wicket and collects a couple.

Drinks. Only a matter of time before India Under-19 officially book their place in the final. It has been a brilliant game for them and they would want to finish it soon now by picking up these 3 wickets.
Full and outside off, Shaw strokes it to sweeper cover for a single.
Shortish and around off, Shaw stays back and looks to steer it down but gets a bottom edge. The ball falls near the stumps and he looks for a run. Turned down.

FOUR! Short in length and around off, Shaw gets on top of the bounce and pulls it over the leaping mid-wicket fielder. It races behind and the deep fielder tries his best to pull it back with a dive. He though fails to do so cleanly and after confirming with the third umpire, it's given as a boundary.
Short and following the batsman down the leg side, at 134 kph, Jack steps back to power it through the line but only manages an inside edge. It rolls to the right side of the keeper and they cross.
Fullish and around off, Shaw opens the face of his bat and pushes it with soft hands to deep point. His call is for two but then he decides to settle for a single.
Extra bounce and it beats the outside edge. Short and around off, Lachlan Shaw hangs his bat out to dry and gets beaten.
Rajvardhan Hangargekar (5-1-17-0) is back on.
Fetches a full ball from outside off and sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Floated and full around off, pushed back defensively to the bowler.
Wide! Very short and very wide outside off, Shaw shuffles across to cut but misses.
Walks down the track to a full ball and forces it down to long off for a run.
Wide! Spinning down the leg side, Sinfield attempts to flick but misses. A good take by the keeper.
Oohhh...that missed the off stump by a whisker. Floated and full around off, spinning in, Jack tries to heave again but misses.
FOUR! That's a pretty safe shot! Loopy and full, turning in from around off, Jack Sinfield goes down on one knee and slog-sweeps it with the spin for a boundary at deep mid-wicket.
Flatter and on off, punched off the back foot to covers.

DROPPED AND FOUR! Would have been a stunning catch. Flighted delivery, full and around middle, Shaw sweeps it firmly and aerially towards short fine leg where the fielder dives to his left but it deflects off his hands and goes behind for a boundary.
Goes on the back foot and punches it to sweeper cover for one.
Flatter and shorter around off, Jack Sinfield drags his attempted heave to wide long on. The fielder in the deep fumbles and they get the second run.
Wide! Turning down the leg side, Jack Sinfield tries to pull but misses.
Floated and outside off, Jack covers his sticks and allows it through.
Fuller and on off, driven down to long on for a run.
That's an interesting shot selection. Full and floated around off, turning away, Shaw tries to be adventurous with his reverse-batted shot but fails to connect.
Jack Sinfield walks out to bat.

OUT! BOWLED! Another wicket to a spinner. Flatter and around off, an arm ball, skidding straight on, Tobias Snell is hesitant to commit himself forward, stays back and tries to force it out but misses. The off stump is pegged back. End is nigh for Australia Under-19.
Fuller and on off, pushed off the front foot to covers.
Works a full ball to mid-wicket and collects a single.
Strides forward and drives it in front of square on the off side for a run.
Tossed up and outside off, left alone.

Direct hit would have been curtains for Lachlan Shaw! Flatter and shorter around off, Snell moves back and eases it to deep mid-wicket. They attempt for the second run as the fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. Had the bowler collected, it would have been interesting.
Fuller and on middle, defended off the inner half to short mid-wicket.
The batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.
Misses! Loopy and full outside off, Shaw tries to sweep but misses.

Tough chance! That went to the fielder very quickly. Flatter and around off, a touch short, Tobias Snell goes back to punch but it takes a thick outside edge. The first slip fielder reacts but it hits his left knee and dies down. It rolls away to backward point and the batters cross.
Floated and full on middle, knocked down to long on for one.
Flighted and full around off, Shaw drives it to covers and sends his partner back.
Tobias Snell is the new batter. Also, Rajvardhan Hangargekar is taken off after that 9-run over and Nishant Sindhu is back on.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Yet another Aussie batter loses his wicket to a spinner! Trial by turn is turning out to be very costly for them! Loopy ball, around off. William Salzmann looks to work it away to the leg side but ends up chipping it back to the bowler. Vicky Ostwal takes the easiest of return catches.
Shorter, outside off. Shaw slaps it to sweeper cover for one.
Now dances down the track and drills it towards long off for one.
Shorter, on off. William Salzmann blocks it from the crease.
Dropped short, lands on off and turns away. William Salzmann misses the cut.
Tap and run. Flatter, on off. Shaw blocks it towards short cover for a quick single.
Banged in short, around off. Shaw worked it past backward point for a single. 9 from that over. A good one for the Aussies.
FOUR! Thrashed away! Length and outside off. Shaw smacks it over covers and the ball races to the fence. The Aussies need a lot more of these.
Short and down the leg side. Shaw misses the pull. Wide called.
Short and outside off. Shaw toe-ends the cut shot towards short cover.
Back of a length, on off. Shaw plays it towards cover.
Length ball, on middle and leg. William gets his bat down low enough to work it past square leg for one.
Fired full and outside off. A lovely drive by William Salzmann to the right of sweeper cover for a couple.
India Under-19 feeding some pace now. Rajvardhan Hangargekar is back into the attack. 0/8 in his 4 overs so far, has a maiden against him also.
Vicky bowls the arm ball now, landing on off and coming back with the angle. William Salzmann goes back and across and then pushes it through covers for one.
This time comes down the track and pushes it to the left of the bowler. Vicky dives but fails to stop it. It goes to long off for one.
Loopy ball, around off. Shaw puts in a stride to block it.
Fuller, around off. Shaw looks to work it away but gets the leading edge to mid off.
Shorter, on off. William Salzmann taps it to short mid-wicket for one.
Darted on middle. Played back to the bowler.
Now Shaw comes down the track and plays it to short cover. The required rate has gone over 8 now.
William Salzmann dances down the track to drive but gets the outside edge. The ball goes past the diving point fielder for one.
A single as this full ball is worked to long on.
Fuller, on the pads. Blocked out.
BEAUTY! Sindhu drags his length back, bowls it slow and on off. Shaw gets forward to block but it turns and goes past the outside edge.
Nicely looped up, on off. Shaw blocks it well.
Shorter, around off. Guided towards point.
Vicky drops it short, outside off. William Salzmann cuts it to backward point.
Loopy ball, on off. William Salzmann drives it straight to short cover.
A single as Shaw pushes this full ball to sweeper cover.
Vicky Ostwal bowls it short, quick and outside off. Shaw misses the cut.
Shaw comes down the track and pushes this to short cover.
Full and on the pads. Worked to short fine leg.
William Salzmann is the new batsman.

OUT! BOWLED! WHAT A RIPPER! Sindhu bowls it really slow, wide outside off and a bit short. Nivethan Radhakrishnan hangs his bat out to dry and leaves a big gap between the bat and the pad. You could drive a bus through that gap. The ball turns back in sharply, clips the inside edge and goes back to hit the stumps.
Tossed up, wide outside off. Nivethan Radhakrishnan gets low and drives it aerially towards sweeper cover. The fielder cuts it off and two runs are taken. 100 up!
Shorter, around the pads. Shaw works it towards square leg. The fielder dives to his left and keeps it to one.
Nivethan Radhakrishnan dances down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it to long off for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Shaw guides it to the right of point and takes a quick single.
A defensive push back to the bowler ends the over. The required rate is 7.5 now.
Nicely tossed up, on off. Nivethan Radhakrishnan looks to hit it down the ground but gets the inside edge back on the pads.
Loopy ball, on the pads. A nice block by Nivethan Radhakrishnan. India Under-19 won't mind this one bit.
Tossed up, wide outside off. Shaw reaches out and drives it to sweeper cover for one.
Shorter and outside off. Nivethan Radhakrishnan goes back in his crease and cuts it towards deep cover for one.
Darted on the pads. Nivethan Radhakrishnan plays it back towards the bowler.
Kaushal Tambe is back into the attack. 0/16 in his 4 overs so far.
Shorter, around off. Punched towards cover-point for a single.
Darted on the pads. Shaw misses the flick and gets pinged on the pads. The ball rolls past the keeper and they get a leg bye.
A single as this full ball is worked to long on.

FOUR! Edged but a boundary for Nivethan Radhakrishnan! Tossed up, wide outside off. He goes for the drive but gets the outside edge. It runs past short third man. The fielder chases it but cannot get there.
Tossed up, wide outside off. Nivethan Radhakrishnan guides it to backward point.
Loopy ball, on off. Played back to the bowler.
Shaw drives this full ball down the ground but Ostwal dives to his left to stop it.
Darted on off. Shaw digs it back to the bowler.
Fuller, on off. Pushed past cover for one.
Short and outside off. Shaw slaps it to deep cover for one.
Loopy ball, on off. Punched back to the bowler.
Shorter and outside off. Shaw slaps it wide of deep point. He wants the second and sprints back for it. Shaw loses his bat near the batting crease but makes it back in as the throw is a bit wild.
Ripper! Shorter, starts outside off and turns back in sharply. Nivethan Radhakrishnan looks to cut but the ball goes past his bat and just past the off pole.
Nivethan Radhakrishnan walks in next.

OUT! TAKEN! A dolly and Shaik Rasheed won't drop those! Australia Under-19 lose their skipper and they are in deep trouble now! Tossed up, on off. He goes for the sweep but Nishant Sindhu gets the ball to turn and also gets a bit of extra bounce. It takes the top edge and flies towards backward square leg. Shaik Rasheed takes it with ease by moving across to his right from short fine leg. 208 runs needed in 175 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Shaik Rasheed b Nishant Sindhu

Commentary.Commentary: Nice turn there! It's tossed up, lands outside off and turns back in sharply. Cooper Connolly looks to block but gets the inside edge.
A single as this is worked past mid-wicket.
Nishant Sindhu is also getting some purchase from the surface.
Flatter, around off. Blocked out.
Turn and bounce! Flatter, lands on off and turns away. Shaw gets hit high on the back thigh while looking to block.
Fullish and on middle, Shaw shows a straight bat and plays it to long on for the fifth single of this over.
Floated and full outside off, Cooper Connolly strokes it to deep cover for another run.
Uses his feet to come down the track and eases a full ball to long on for a run.
Nicely tossed up, some drift in the air as it lands full around off, Cooper Connolly gets forward and bunts it to long off for one.
The length is short, on off, Shaw goes back and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Flighted and on off, Shaw stays back and defends it to the off side.
Excellent fielding. Short and around off, Cooper Connolly forces it off his back foot and the short mid-wicket fielder makes a diving stop to his right.
Leans forward and pushes it to deep cover for another run.
Flatter and shorter on off, Shaw punches off the back foot to mid-wicket.
Loopy and full outside off, Cooper Connolly drives this time, in front of square on the off side, and collects a single.
Flighted and full outside off, Lachlan Shaw drives this time, past the diving cover fielder, for a single.
Fuller and outside off, Shaw tries to drive but misses.
Arm ball around off, Shaw goes back and punches it to long off for a run.
Loopy and around off, Shaw gets forward and defends it from the outer portion of his bat.
Flatter and on off, Shaw defends it off his back foot.
Lachlan Shaw walks out to bat. He dropped the catch of Shaik Rasheed when the latter was in his early 20s. Can he redeem himself?

OUT! CAUGHT! That's soft, as soft as butter. Turn and bounce for Vicky Ostwal. He lands it a touch short around off and the ball stops a bit too as it approaches the batter. Campbell Kellaway goes on the back foot to deal with it but only manages to check his shot. The ball flies tamely off the middle of his bat towards short mid-wicket where Nishant Sindhu takes a simple catch. Australia Under-19 are in trouble now, they have lost their top three.
Commentary.Howout: c Nishant Sindhu b Vicky Ostwal

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and quicker on off, spinning in, Campbell defends it back.
A soft outside edge. Tossed up, outside off and fuller in length, Campbell Kellaway lunges to defend but it takes the outer half and races past first slip for a couple of runs.
Change. Vicky Ostwal is on now.
A touch short and on off, Cooper defends it from the back foot to the off side. A successful over from Angkrish Raghuvanshi.
Goes on the back foot and forces it to covers.
Fuller around leg, defended.

Drinks! A big moment in the game as it was this pair that kept the scoreboard moving for Australia Under-19. But now, with the spinners operating, the new batter may find it tough. Cooper Connolly walks out to bat with a big responsibility on his shoulders. Australia Under-19 need 220 in 201 and they need a big stand now.

OUT! Adjudged LBW! India Under-19 have their second breakthrough and it's a big strike. Smart bowling from Angkrish Raghuvanshi. He lets out a slider around off, the ball lands and skids on with the angle. Miller sits inside the crease like a dead duck as he attempts to work it around. He misses and is pinged on the front pad. They appeal and the finger goes up almost immediately. No doubt there. The 68-run stand is broken and Australia Under-19 will have to rebuild.
Again it's short and on off, Kellaway goes on the back foot and punches it to long off for one.
Flatter and shorter on off, Corey goes back and strokes it to deep cover for a run.
Fuller and around off, Miller prods forward and drives it through covers for a run. Four singles from the over.
Skidding in from around off, Campbell Kellaway goes back and works it in front of square leg for one.
Fuller and on off, driven through the line but straight to the bowler.
Slower through the air, full and around off, Miller taps it down to the left of backward point for a single.
Fullish and on middle, Campbell nudges it down through mid on for one.
Fuller and close to off, Campbell Kellaway leans forward and defends it to covers.
Around off, a slider, Corey goes on the back foot and presents a straight bat in defense.
Short and on off, forced to deep cover for a run.
Misfield! Loopy and full around off, Campbell Kellaway flicks it to mid-wicket where the fielder slips and lets it through. They take two.
Presses forward to a full ball and pushes it to covers.
Wide! Quicker one, skidding down the leg side, the batter tries to flick but misses. It hits the pads of the keeper and deflects to short fine leg.
Very full again, around off, it's eased down to long off for another single.
Loopy and full around off, Campbell Kellaway is forward as he strokes it down to long off for a run.
Change. Angkrish Raghuvanshi to roll his arm over now.
Flighted and a touch short on off, Miller pushes it back to the bowler to complete the 14th over. The required rate is 6.44 now.
Goes on the front foot and hits it in the gap at cover-point for a quick run.
Floated and full on middle, drifting in, Campbell Kellaway leans and defends it near his front pad.
Tambe drags his length short again, outside off, it's cut to deep point for one.
Shortish and on off, punched down to long off for a run.
Flighted and on off, defended back off the front foot.

EDGY FOUR! Raj Angad Bawa hurls across a length ball outside off, Corey Miller pushes inside the line and gets a fat outside edge behind. It beats the diving keeper and the diving third man fielder to find the fence. The 50-run stand comes up!
Perhaps the slower one. On a length around off, Miller defends it back to the bowler.
Full and wide outside off, Miller chases but mistimes it from the bottom half of the bat to mid off.

FOUR! Great timing and placement! Miller is looking in fine touch. Width there around off, on a length and angling away, Corey Miller stays on the back foot and steers it in the gap at backward point for a boundary - his fifth of the innings. 50 up!
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it back in the direction of the bowler.
In the zone outside off, on a length and angling further away, Miller has nothing to do with it.
Quicker and flatter on off, Miller moves back and turns it in the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it with gentle hands to cover-point.
A long hop around off, skidding in, Campbell moves back and punches it to wide long off for a single.
Loopy and full outside off, Miller strokes it to sweeper cover for one.
Drags his length short and delivers it on middle, Campbell Kellaway goes back and punches it to long on for a single.
Tossed up, full and on off, defended back to the bowler.
Fractionally short and on off, angling away, Corey stays back and taps it down to backward point. This stand is worth 41, slow going but they are building a good platform.
FOUR! Wow, gorgeous! This is overpitched alright but it still has to be put away. Corey Miller leans into the drive and caresses it down the ground for a boundary. No chance for mid off.

Fullish and around off, Kellaway drives it down the ground and to the left of mid off. Campbell Kellaway is a bit late in taking off but then rushes across. The fielder picks up the ball and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. The keeper collects at the other end and advises the fielder to target the base of the stumps.
Serves it on a length and around off, Campbell Kellaway stays back and punches it to short cover. The fielder there makes a partial stop.
Bawa pulls his length back and digs it in short, around off, Campbell Kellaway goes on the back foot and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Pitches it up and outside off, inviting the drive, Campbell Kellaway gets forward to drive but only manages to slice it along the ground to backward point.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over.

Miller again cuts a wide one but straight towards the man at covers. Australia Under-19 are marginally ahead of where India Under-19 were at the end of Powerplay 1. The Aussies are at 37 for 1 while the Indians had scored 34 for 1.
Fuller, on off. Blocked out.
FOUR! A bit of width and punished! Shorter, outside off. Miller rocks back and cuts it through covers for a boundary.
Darted on off. Miller stays in the crease to block it.
Shorter, on off. Campbell Kellaway clips it past mid-wicket for one.
Tambe starts with a flatter one, on off. Played back to the bowler.
Another change in bowling. Kaushal Tambe to bowl his offies.
It's fired fuller and down the leg side. Miller goes for the flick but doesn't connect. The ball though takes something on its way and bounces in front of the keeper.
On a length, around off. Pushed to covers.
Third man comes in and point is pushed back.
Full and outside off. Miller goes for the drive but gets the inside edge back on the pads.

Short of a length, outside off. Campbell Kellaway chops it away. The man at cover-point, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, dives to his left and stops it. There is a bit of hesitation but the batters take a single.
Through the gaps! Length and outside off. This is driven nicely through the gap at covers. The two fielders chase it and keep it to a couple.
On a length, angling across off. Kellaway plants his front foot forward and plays it to point.
Length and down the leg side. Campbell Kellaway misses the flick. Good carry on that as Dinesh Bana collects it in front of his face. Wide called.
Raj Angad Bawa is introduced into the attack.
FOUR! No need to sprint for that one! Overpitched and outside off, Miller puts in a stride and thumps it past extra cover for a boundary.
Tap and run! Shorter, around off. Campbell Kellaway plays it with soft hands towards covers and the batters sprint away for a single.
Back of a length, sliding down the leg side. Miller helps it to fine leg for one.
Right on the money. Length and on middle, Miller chooses to block it back to Kumar.
Length and on the body. Played towards deep square leg for an easy single.
Play and a miss again! Kumar lands it full and outside off. Campbell Kellaway is tempted and goes for a booming drive. He misses though.
Play and a miss! Rajvardhan Hangargekar serves it full and wide outside off. Miller doesn't move his feet and goes for the drive. The ball zips past the outside edge.
Short but quite wide. Miller leaves it.
Dug short, on off. Campbell Kellaway pulled it to deep square leg for one.

Edged but safe! Nice and full, around off. Miller goes for the drive but gets the outside edge. The ball goes wide of the diving second slip fielder and travels towards third man. The man in the deep dives to his right and keeps it to one.
A bit fuller, but right on the off pole line. Miller stays solid in his defense of this one.
Length ball, around off. A nice drive by Miller but straight towards mid off.
Kumar drags his length back and bowls a length ball, on off. It's blocked out by Campbell Kellaway from the crease.
FOUR! Top shot! A treat to the eyes! Overpitched, on middle and leg. Campbell Kellaway drives it straight down the ground for a boundary. Lovely extension of the arms there.
Full, on off. Miller looks to block but he too gets an outside edge. The ball goes to third man for a run.
Nice and full, outside off. Inviting Campbell Kellaway for the drive and he goes for it. It takes the outside edge though and runs away to third man for one.
Again, on a length, on the stumps. Kellaway blocks it to the left of the bowler now.
Appeal for LBW! Length ball, landing around middle and angling down. Campbell Kellaway is struck high on the pads while looking to work it away. It was too high so the appeal is turned down.
Change of angle as Rajvardhan Hangargekar comes 'round the wicket. He bowls a length ball, but this is wide enough for Miller to cover his stumps and leave it.
Bowls it on a length, around off. Campbell Kellaway looks to drive it down the ground but gets it off the outer half towards covers for one.
Full and wide outside off. Miller reaches out for it and tries to drive. He ends up scuffing his shot in the air and it falls in no man's land at covers. They cross for a single.
A bumper, angling across off. Miller sways away from it.
A low full toss, on off. Miller looks to drive it but gets it off the inner half past square leg for a couple.
Beaten! Fuller, lands outside off and angles further away. Miller is beaten as he looks to block.
Well bowled! Just wide outside off, on a length. Kellaway thinks about blocking but pulls out in the end.
Full again, right on the off pole line. This time, Campbell Kellaway gets his bat down in time to play it back to the bowler.
Full, on the fifth-stump line. Left alone again.
Kumar bowls it closer to the off pole line but wide enough for Campbell Kellaway to leave it with ease.
Full, lands wide outside off and shapes away. Campbell Kellaway has no qualms in leaving it.
Full and down the leg side. Tucked to fine leg for one by Miller.

A screeching yorker to end the over! Just around off and Campbell Kellaway fails to dig it out. The keeper collects it and there is an appeal by the Indian players but turned down. Quite surprising that it neither took the edge nor the off stump.
Back of a length, outside off. Pushed to covers.
Rajvardhan Hangargekar fires it full now, on off. Campbell Kellaway brings his bat down and offers the full face to block it.
Sharp and short, outside off. Kellaway sways away from the line.
Shorter again, angling across off. It's punched off the back foot but the man at short cover moves to his left and stops any thought for a quick single.
Back of a length, around off. Kellaway hops and blocks it to the off side.
Nice and full, on off. Pushed to cover. End of a successful over for Kumar.
Too full and down the leg side. Miller misses the flick. Wide called.
Length, around off. Miller looks to block but gets it off the outer half of his bat to point.
On a length, slipping on the pads. Miller blocks it out.
FOUR! Oh, glorious! A bit too full and a bit too wide. Miller gets forward and drives it handsomely through covers for a boundary.
Fuller and outside off. Miller taps it to covers.
Corey Miller walks in next at number 3. He scored a handy knock against Pakistan Under-19 but otherwise has not got enough opportunity to bat.

OUT! LBW! Ravi Kumar lands it well and gets the first wicket for India Under-19! A peach of a delivery and the in-form Teague Wyllie has to walk back. Kumar bowls it full and fast, it lands around leg and swings back in late. Wyllie looks to work it away but gets rapped on the pads. There is a huge appeal and up goes the finger. Kumar draws first blood and it's a massive blow to Australia Under-19 as the boy with 250-plus runs in the tournament is on his bike.
Starts with a full and very wide one. Wyllie leaves it alone.
Ravi Kumar to operate from the opposite end. His left-arm angle will challenge the Aussies. One slip in place...
Now, Teague Wyllie gets off the mark. He leans forward and plays this full ball to covers for a quick single.
A sharp and short one, outside off. This is left alone by Teague Wyllie.

Rajvardhan Hangargekar pulls out as he loses the ball. He got too close to the stumps and clipped the left elbow of the umpire as he shapes up to deliver. That would have hurt the umpire. Bring on the elbow guard.
The chase is underway! Shorter, down the leg side. Campbell Kellaway helps it to fine leg for one.
Length ball, lands outside off and comes back in with the angle. Campbell pushes it to covers.
Shorter again, but on off. Campbell Kellaway clips it towards square leg. He needs to watch out for the one that Rajvardhan Hangargekar will fire full.
Some aggression as Rajvardhan Hangargekar digs it short but wide enough outside off for Campbell Kellaway to leave it with ease.
